subject: Literacy
title: Our literacy celebration
objectives: Children will show Year learning through games and stations.
Teachers will complete every child’s end-of-year record and transition note.
content: Revising listening, rhymes and sounds, stories and books, and celebrating the year with end-of-year records and a transition note.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly; record what children can do; invite parents to the celebration; complete the transition note honestly for the next teacher.
learnerActivities: Show what they know through games and stations and enjoy a literacy celebration.
resources: Songs and rhymes from the year
Books, name cards and story boxes
assessment: Observe and record each child’s end-of-year literacy learning and complete the transition note.
expectedOutcomes: Takes part confidently in familiar literacy games.
Each child has an end-of-year observation record.

lessons.title: Revising listening, rhymes and sounds
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit sound games, rhymes and the four sounds s, a, t and p.
successCriteria: Says at least two of the four sounds
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, speaking, rhymes, stories, early sounds, mark-making, names and books across the year.
lessons.starter: Ring the bell and say "Shh, listen." Say "Today we play our favourite sound and rhyme games."
teacherActivities: Play listening statues with the bell.
Sing a favourite rhyme and pause for the last word.
Play the sound sort game with sss, a, t and p.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
learnerActivities: Children sort by first sound with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play listening statues with the bell. Children: Children stop and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing a favourite rhyme and pause for the last word. Children: Children finish the rhyme.
Step 3. Teacher: Play the sound sort game with sss, a, t and p. Children: Children sort by first sound with support.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Sound and rhyme games
steps: Children play each game for four minutes.
The teacher notes which sounds each child can say.
practical.safety: Keep sounds gentle and the floor clear. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use two sounds.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sound does the snake make?

lessons.conclusion: Ring the bell and say "Good listening."
lessons.homeConnection: Play sound and rhyme games at home during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit sound games, rhymes and the four sounds s, a, t and p" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising stories and books
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit stories, books and their own books.
successCriteria: Shares a book with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, speaking, rhymes, stories, early sounds, mark-making, names and books across the year.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us visit our stories and our books today." Open the story box.
teacherActivities: Tell a favourite story with props.
Put three picture cards in order and tell the story.
Let each child choose a favourite book to look at.
learnerActivities: Child shares their book with a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell a favourite story with props. Children: Children join in and retell.
Step 2. Teacher: Put three picture cards in order and tell the story. Children: Child orders and tells.
Step 3. Teacher: Share the books they made. Children: Child shares their book with a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite book to look at. Children: Child chooses and turns pages.

practical.title: Story and book time
steps: Set up the story box and book corner.
The teacher notes retelling and book handling.
practical.safety: Supervise props and books. Keep floors clear and cushions tidy.

differentiation.support: Sit with the child and point to pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story to a younger friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the books away and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Read together every day during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit stories, books and their own books" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Play stations for the year
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s literacy learning across the year at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows listening, speaking, sound and mark-making skills
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, speaking, rhymes, stories, early sounds, mark-making, names and books across the year.
lessons.starter: Sing the hello song and show six stations to the class.
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: sounds, rhymes, stories, books, names and marks.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: sounds, rhymes, stories, books, names and marks. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Six stations
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and materials large and soft.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: listens; says s, a, t and p; joins in rhymes; retells a story; finds their name; makes marks and lines.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite game from this year at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s literacy learning across the year at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Literacy celebration
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will celebrate the year with songs, rhymes, stories and their own books.
successCriteria: Shares their book with an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, speaking, rhymes, stories, early sounds, mark-making, names and books across the year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate everything we learned. Let us sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions.
Invite children to show their book to a visitor or parent.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Invite children to show their book to a visitor or parent. Children: Child shares their book.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sit in a circle with visitors.
Sing, share books and say each name.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise visitors and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and share a book together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s end-of-year literacy record from the year’s observations. Record the child’s strengths and a next step for Nursery 1.

questions.question: What do you like about your book?

expectedOutcomes: Enjoys songs, rhymes, stories and books
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Nursery 1."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep singing, sharing books and playing sound games during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate the year with songs, rhymes, stories and their own books" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Transition note and records
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 1 teacher.
successCriteria: Records what each child can do
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, speaking, rhymes, stories, early sounds, mark-making, names and books across the year.
lessons.starter: Today the children enjoy free play with familiar materials while the teacher completes the transition notes.
teacherActivities: Set out free play with books, instruments, dough and puppets.
Review each child’s three term records and portfolio.
Complete the note: strengths, interests, language, sounds known and next steps.
learnerActivities: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Children play and talk with the helper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set out free play with books, instruments, dough and puppets. Children: Children play freely and happily.
Step 2. Teacher: Review each child’s three term records and portfolio. Children: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete the note: strengths, interests, language, sounds known and next steps. Children: Children play and talk with the helper.

practical.title: Free play and records
steps: Set out four play areas with a helper.
The teacher reviews records at a quiet table.
The teacher completes each transition note.
practical.safety: A second adult must supervise play while the teacher completes the notes. Keep all areas safe and tidy.

differentiation.support: Offer familiar toys and a helper nearby.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to help a friend tidy up.

assessment.method: Write for each child: what they can do in listening, speaking, rhymes, sounds, early reading and mark-making; their interests; any support needed; and a next step. Use the four-level scale and facts you have seen.

questions.question: What do you like to play?
What did you learn this year?

expectedOutcomes: Has a transition note for each child
lessons.conclusion: Tidy up together and say goodbye to the year.
lessons.homeConnection: Share the end-of-year report with your child and keep reading together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 1 teacher" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
